datasets.title: Namibia: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/nam-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

entity.name: Copernicus / European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC)

lineage.description: FAPAR values from VIIRS satellite observations are collected in 10-day time composites. Anomalies are calculated at each grid cell as the deviation from a long-term mean baseline spanning 2012 to the most recent complete year, enabling detection and monitoring of agricultural drought impacts on vegetation greenness and productivity across Namibia.

sources.name: Copernicus / European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.description: VIIRS satellite-derived FAPAR biophysical measurements processed into 10-day composites and anomaly calculations to provide operational drought monitoring data for vegetation assessment
